title: PMFBY Operational Guidelines — Claims, Premium & Timelines
content:
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is the Government of India's crop insurance scheme, providing financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests or diseases.

Premium: Farmers pay a uniform premium of 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial and horticultural crops. The balance premium is shared between the central and state governments, with no upper limit on government subsidy.

Enrollment: Enrollment is voluntary for all farmers as of the current scheme guidelines. Loanee farmers (those who have taken a crop loan) may be enrolled by their bank/PACS; non-loanee farmers can enroll through the PMFBY portal, Common Service Centres, or authorised insurance intermediaries, within the notified cut-off date for each crop season, generally before sowing.

What is covered: Yield losses due to natural fire, lightning, storm, hailstorm, cyclone, flood, inundation, landslide, drought, dry spells, pests and diseases. Post-harvest losses are covered for up to 14 days after harvest for crops kept in 'cut and spread' condition, for specific perils like unseasonal rain. Localized risks such as hailstorm and landslide are covered on an individual farm basis.

Claim process: In case of crop loss from a localized risk (hailstorm, landslide, inundation) or post-harvest loss, the farmer must inform the insurance company or the concerned bank/agriculture department within 72 hours of the event, through the crop insurance app, toll-free helpline, or written intimation to the nearest agriculture office. For widespread calamities, claims are assessed through Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) conducted by the state government across the notified area, and claims are paid to all farmers in that area based on the shortfall between actual and threshold yield — no individual intimation is needed in this case.

Settlement timeline: As per scheme guidelines, claims are to be settled within a defined period after yield data is received from the state government, typically within 2 months of the completion of the crop-cutting experiments. Delays attract interest to be paid by the insurance company to the farmer.

Documents needed: Aadhaar card, land ownership or tenancy/sharecropper proof, bank account details linked to Aadhaar, and sowing certificate where required. Tenant farmers and sharecroppers are eligible on production of a valid tenancy or cultivation agreement as recognised by the state.

Grievance redressal: A farmer whose claim is delayed, denied, or disputed can approach the District Level Grievance Redressal Committee, contact the insurance company's toll-free number, or raise the issue on the PMFBY portal/app. Persistent disputes can be escalated to the State Level Coordination Committee on Crop Insurance.
